english.title: 10 West End Musicals Worth Travelling to London For
english.excerpt: Oya Canli shares 10 West End musicals worth travelling to London for — from timeless classics to contemporary West End favourites.
english.body:
As someone who happily travels for live theatre, I'd love to share a few of my favourite West End productions that I believe every musical lover should experience at least once.

London's West End has long been considered one of the world's greatest theatre destinations, attracting millions of visitors every year. While many productions eventually tour internationally, there's something truly special about seeing them in the city they call home. Historic theatres, exceptional casts, breathtaking productions and an electric atmosphere combine to create an experience that's difficult to replicate anywhere else.

Whether you're planning your very first theatre trip or your tenth visit to London, these are ten musicals that deserve a place on your itinerary.

### 1. Les Misérables
If there is one musical that defines the West End, it is Les Misérables. Having played in London since 1985, Claude-Michel Schönberg and Alain Boublil's adaptation of Victor Hugo's novel continues to move audiences with its unforgettable score and emotional storytelling.

From "I Dreamed a Dream" to "One Day More," every performance is special. The Sondheim Theatre has become synonymous with this legendary production, making London the ultimate place to experience this masterpiece.
Don't miss if you love: epic stories, history, unforgettable music and emotional performances.

### 2. The Phantom of the Opera
This is for capturing theatrical magic. Andrew Lloyd Webber's masterpiece has enchanted audiences for decades with its soaring melodies, lavish costumes and unforgettable staging.

Seeing the Phantom emerge beneath the Paris Opera House or hearing the title song and "The Music of the Night" performed live is something every musical lover should experience at least once.
Perfect for: romantics, lovers of classic musicals and anyone who appreciates spectacular theatre.

### 3. Moulin Rouge! The Musical
Walking into the Piccadilly Theatre already feels like entering the famous Parisian nightclub. Rich red velvet, glittering chandeliers and extravagant décor set the mood before the orchestra even begins.

Once the curtain rises, audiences are treated to spectacular choreography, dazzling costumes and an energetic soundtrack featuring dozens of contemporary pop hits seamlessly woven into the story.
This is theatre on the grandest scale. 

### 4. The Lion King
Disney's The Lion King continues to amaze audiences with Julie Taymor's revolutionary puppetry and costume design. The opening scene alone remains one of the most breathtaking moments in musical theatre.
It's an artistic achievement that leaves audiences of every age speechless.

### 5. Hadestown
For those looking for something different, Hadestown offers one of the most original musical experiences currently in London.

Inspired by Greek mythology and infused with folk, jazz and blues, it tells the tragic love story of Orpheus and Eurydice while exploring themes of hope, sacrifice and resilience. It's intimate, poetic and utterly captivating.

### 6. Hamilton
Lin-Manuel Miranda's groundbreaking work combines hip-hop, rap, jazz and traditional Broadway influences to tell the story of Alexander Hamilton in an entirely fresh way.
Its energy, clever lyrics and inventive staging continue to attract audiences from around the world.

### 7. Wicked
Long before Dorothy arrived in Oz, there was the remarkable friendship between Elphaba and Glinda.

Wicked has become one of the West End's biggest successes thanks to its spectacular score, emotional storytelling and the iconic anthem "Defying Gravity." Even if you know The Wizard of Oz, this story offers an entirely new perspective.

### 8. MAMMA MIA!
Set on a beautiful Greek island and featuring ABBA's greatest hits, MAMMA MIA! remains one of London's most joyful evenings out. It is impossible not to leave the theatre smiling.

### 9. The Devil Wears Prada
Fashion meets musical theatre in this stylish adaptation of Lauren Weisberger's bestselling novel.

Featuring original music by Elton John, glamorous costumes and plenty of humour, this relatively new addition to the West End has quickly become one of London's most talked-about productions.

### 10. Matilda The Musical
Tim Minchin's witty songs and Dennis Kelly's clever adaptation have transformed Roald Dahl's beloved story into one of the finest family musicals ever created.
Filled with imagination, humour and heart, Matilda proves that children's stories can deliver powerful messages for adults too. It is fun to watch it with kids as well.

## Why London?
People often ask why they should travel to London when many of these musicals tour internationally.

The answer lies in the experience itself.

West End theatres are part of theatre history. Many productions were created specifically for these venues, performed by exceptional casts and supported by some of the world's finest creative teams. You simply become part of a tradition that has inspired audiences for generations.

For theatre lovers, a visit to the West End is a journey into one of the world's great cultural capitals.

## Final Curtain
Every time I visit London's West End, I'm reminded why I keep coming back. It's about the anticipation before the lights go down, the incredible (INCREDIBLE!!!) talent on stage, and the feeling of sharing an unforgettable experience with an audience that loves theatre just as much as I do.

Whether you're drawn to timeless classics like Les Misérables and The Phantom of the Opera, contemporary masterpieces such as Hamilton and Hadestown, or feel-good favourites like MAMMA MIA!, I hope this guide inspires you to plan your own West End adventure.

Because if there's one thing I've learned after countless trips to London's theatres is that some musicals really are worth booking a flight for. And once you've experienced the magic of the West End, you'll already be dreaming about your next visit: not just for another musical, but to immerse yourself once again in London's extraordinary theatre culture.
